title: Philadelphia’s tide, a century apart
summary: Early (1915–1935) versus modern (2000–2020) tide at Philadelphia. With the same tide and sea level, the changed M2 and M4 constituents alone keep water above MHHW for 2.3 h instead of 1.5 h.

title: First-author poster at the AGU Annual Meeting 2025
place: American Geophysical Union Annual Meeting (AGU25), New Orleans, Louisiana
summary: “Localized Decline in Tidal Overtides Reveals Anthropogenic Smoothing of the Delaware Estuary”, with Taznin Naher, Jorge Lorenzo-Trueba, Stefan Talke, Thomas Wahl, Sönke Dangendorf and colleagues. A century of deepening, shoreline hardening and marsh loss has weakened the nonlinear tidal overtides, shifting the Delaware Estuary into a different tidal regime.
captions: Presenting my first-author poster on tidal overtides in the Delaware Estuary at AGU25, New Orleans.

title: Physical & Natural Sciences Responsible Conduct of Research
Reflections from the next generation of climate researchers
summary: [Md Nurul Kadir,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/md-nurul-kadir/) a dedicated MACH researcher from the [University of Florida](https://geology.ufl.edu/), shares his personal journey into climate science and reflects on the impact of his work. As a MACH team member, Kadir’s research aims to understand how estuarine bathymetry, or underwater topography, affects tidally driven water levels, flood risk and communities.
